title: [.NET / iOS 26] C# game crashes ~0.3s after launch in RELEASE builds — RenderingDevice heap corruption trapped by iOS 26's type-aware allocator
body:
### Tested versions
- **Godot 4.6.2.stable.mono.official** — crashes
- **Godot 4.7.1.stable.mono.official** — crashes (bump does **not** fix it)

### System information
- Device: **iPhone 16 Pro (iPhone17,1)**, **iOS 26.5.2** (A18 — software type-aware allocator, *not* opt-in hardware MTE)
- Xcode 26.3 / 26.5, iOS 26 SDK
- .NET SDK 9 (net9.0) and .NET 10 (net10.0) both reproduce
- Export: iOS, **release** (`--export-release`), C# / .NET (mono)

### Issue description
A C#/.NET Godot game exported in **release** crashes **~0.3–5 s after launch on device**. The build succeeds, installs, and launches; then the process is terminated by the iOS 26 allocator's corruption trap.

- `EXC_BREAKPOINT (SIGTRAP)` in `libsystem_malloc _xzm_xzone_malloc_freelist_outlined` — iOS 26's **type-aware `xzone` allocator** detecting a poisoned free block.
- Crash site is on the **main thread**, during the **root Window's first render-target creation**, before any game logic:
  ```
  _xzm_xzone_malloc_freelist_outlined            (iOS 26 malloc corruption trap)
  operator new -> HashMap<RID, HashSet<RID>>
  RenderingDevice::_add_dependency(RID, RID)
  RenderingDevice::texture_create_shared(...)
  RendererRD::TextureStorage::_update_render_target(...)
  RendererViewport::viewport_set_size(...)
  Window::_update_viewport_size() -> Window::_notification()
  -[GDTViewRenderer setupView:] -[GDTView drawView]
  ```
- **No .NET/mono frames on the crashing thread** — the corruption is detected here but written earlier (classic heap corruption; detection site ≠ cause).

#### Key characteristic — it's a layout-sensitive heisenbug
| Configuration | Result |
|---|---|
| **Release** build (optimized) | **crash** |
| Debug build | runs clean |
| Guard Malloc (`libgmalloc`) | no corruption crash (layout changes) |
| **GDScript** project (no .NET) | runs clean |
| Trivial C# scene (bare Node) | runs clean |
| Minimal code-built 3D SubViewport | runs clean |

Vanishing under debug **and** Guard Malloc is the signature of genuine memory corruption whose manifestation depends on heap layout.

### Minimal reproduction
1. C# / .NET (mono) Godot project.
2. Main scene that instantiates a moderately-populated authored scene (`GameRoot.tscn`: a `VBox` of two `SubViewportContainer`→`SubViewport` regions + chrome) **and** any 3D world (even a bare `Camera3D` node) coexisting.
3. Export **iOS release**, run on an iOS 26 device.

Neither piece alone crashes — only the two coexisting, in release, on iOS 26. (In our project: `GameRoot` scene + `BattleStage3D` in a `SubViewport`.)

#### What we ruled out (does NOT fix it)
- Renderer method (forward_plus / mobile), GPU driver (Metal / Vulkan-MoltenVK)
- `.NET` target (net9 / net10), Godot version (**4.6.2 and 4.7.1**)
- SubViewport hosting vs main-viewport rendering; every SubViewport setting incl. `transparent_bg`, `own_world_3d`, `handle_input_locally`, update mode; viewport resize
- Concurrent GC off (`ConcurrentGarbageCollection=false`)
- Assembly trimming: rooting the game assemblies **and** `GodotSharp` (fully untrimmed builds fail to launch on size, so can't confirm, but rooted-trim still crashes)
- iOS 26 allocator opt-outs: `MallocNanoZone=0`, guard-edges — no effect; no app-level opt-out documented
- Binary SDK-version downgrade (`vtool` → LC_BUILD_VERSION sdk 18.0 + re-sign) — allocator is **OS-version-gated**, not SDK-gated

#### Likely root cause
iOS 26's type-aware `xzone` allocator segregates the heap by allocation type and traps type-confusion. Mono/.NET's GC + native↔managed marshalling do heavy type-punning (reusing memory as different types) that older allocators tolerated. Under **release** trimming/optimization on a moderately-complex C# scene, this trips iOS 26's allocator. Since it reproduces on 4.6.2 **and** 4.7.1, it is not fixed by the current engine; likely needs a fix in Godot's Mono/.NET iOS runtime hosting (or the bundled runtime) for iOS 26 allocator compatibility.

#### Related
- godotengine/godot#89610 (release-only C# crashes, dev builds fine — same shape, pre-iOS-26)
- godotengine/godot#68329 (C# "Heap corruption detected, free list is damaged")
- mono/mono#14364 (native crash in GC due to memory corruption)
- Apple: iOS 26 Memory Integrity / type-aware allocators — https://security.apple.com/blog/memory-integrity-enforcement/
